name: Banded eversion & inversion
summary: Sitting, turn the sole of the foot outward then inward against a band.
setup: Sit with the legs out, band looped around the forefoot and anchored to the side. Keeping the knee still, turn the sole outward against the band (eversion), release; then re-anchor the other way and turn it inward (inversion).
why: The foot rotates about the shin — a movement a phone sees as almost nothing from any angle. Follow the guide and log each direction.
tempo: Turn 1 s, hold 1 s, return 2 s.
contraindications: Pain on the outside of the ankle after a sprain that has not been assessed.

faults.label: Rotating the whole leg
faults.tip: Hold the shin with a hand if needed; only the foot turns.

faults.label: Turning the whole leg
faults.tip: If the thigh rolls, the hip is doing it. Pin the knee and turn only below the ankle.

faults.label: Tiny movements
faults.cue: Turn the foot all the way
faults.tip: Take the sole as far out (or in) as it goes each rep.

faults.label: Letting the band snap back
faults.tip: The slow return is the half most people skip, and the half the ankle needs.

guide.surface: Floor or a chair; band anchored to a table leg.
guide.stop: Sharp pain on the outside or inside of the ankle.
guide.cannotSee: The foot turning — the movement is a rotation the phone cannot resolve.

points.t: Turns fully against the band; knee and shin stay still.
